label: paragraph_title
text: QUEER FISH.

label: text
text:
STRANGE YALMATI
CATCH.

label: text
text: A MERMAID'S CHILD!

label: text
text:
Of the size and appearance of a baby's head, a strange sea-animal was caught by a Shuntung police-man at the ferry wharf. Youmati on Sunday.
HONGKONG, TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 10, 1925.

label: text
text: The description is borne out by a European of about twenty years' standing in the Colony.

label: text
text: Those who saw the "fish" maintain that it must have been a fish as it came out of the water.

label: text
text: It is not correct to say that there was a body as it was all "head," not unlike the head of an infant. The fish had eyes, mouth, nose, ear-holes and fins above the eyes. Another description is that the "fish had a round body, like a California orange."

label: text
text:
A close inspection of the bowl in which the "fish" was kept revealed the fact that the specimen was very much alive. As it breathed and opened its mouth, two tiny teeth could be seen.
Nobody has yet fixed the identity of this extraordinary "fish" but it will be sent to the Museum.
According to the Chinese classics there is a "Kwai" (not Kwei") fish, also known as "Wa Wa," which amounts to a "merbaby" and is able to cry. Possession of such was supposed to bring immense luck.

label: paragraph_title
text: POPPY DAY.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE GREAT DRIVE TO-MORROW

label: text
text: Arrangements are now complete for the great Poppy Day drive to-morrow and having regard to the promises of help received and the amount of keen interest being taken the organisers have every hope of making the day a great success.

label: text
text: It cannot be expected that the tremendous figure collected all over China will be reached this year. That total was almost £1,000 and Hongkong's share was £2,645. It only because little or nothing can be expected from the many towns in China that contributed last year the local organisers are anxious that Hongkong should again do well. If the interest shown bears proportionate results then a successful day can be anticipated for it must be believed that Hongkong is not unconscious of the "debt which still is owing to the survivors of the Great War and their dependants. They are in a sense their country's creditors and it is plainly the duty of all who can to help to pay off a portion of the huge debt that is owing to them.

label: text
text: It is obvious from Earl Haig's cable received a few days ago and published in these columns that the G.H.Q. of the Legion is conscious of the Colony's efforts and grateful for all that has been done. His appeal has been received again and everyone will hope that help will be readily forthcoming.

label: text
text: A fourteen-year old Chinese boy received severe injuries in a motor car accident yesterday.

label: text
text: The ear, which is owned by Lau Sze-yuen, of No. 12, Connaught Road Central, was proceeding along Queen's Road East when the boy ran out from the verandah of a house and was struck on the head, knocking him down.

label: text
text: The driver of the car picked up the injured boy and took him to the Government Civil Hospital.

label: text
text: The Committee appointed to consider ways and means of administering the Trade Loan has made recommendations in respect of certain applications. These have been forwarded to the Government and upon the Government's sanction money will be immediately available.

label: text
text: Unimning "unimpeachable authority," the "Francfurter Zeitung" discloses that Gount von Soden, Chief of the Cabinet of the ex-Crown Prince, Ruyrecht of Bavaria and General Noehl, ex-Commander of the Bavarian Reichswehr, "Division recently visited the members of the Bavarian Government and asked their attitude in the event of

label: text
text:
Rupprecht's proclaiming himself King of Bavaria, adding that the time had come to act and various organisations formed by Noehl were ready.
The Bavarian Government promptly intimated that the proposed step would be regarded as an attempt at revolution and would be opposed by ever-means. It also pointed out that such a coup would inevitably mean the loss of the platyponate.
The pre-republic agents were upon request and informed that master that the time was not yet ripe for the restoration of the Bavarian monarchy.

text: NEW SOLICITOR.

label: text
text: DISTINGUISHED ARMY

label: text
text:
A distinguished Army career is that of Mr. D. L. Shelley, admitted to practice at the Supreme Court this morning. He is attached to G. K. Hall Brutton & Co.
Mr. Shelley, who had practised at Home for a short time, saw the service in 1915 with the Campaign Range in Mesopotamia and on being invalids back to India where he had already served some time previously. He was given a commission in the Indian Army and was Adjuvant with a Punjabis regiment. Shortly after his return to England in 1919 he set up as a saitior on his own in London at Lincoln's Inn and remained there for five years. The practice before was tied on by a

label: text
text:
The Attorney General, Sir Henry Pollock, K.C., referred to this record this morning in applying for his admission on behalf of K. Hall Brutton & Co.
His Honour Mr. Justice H. H. J. Gompertz welcomed Mr. Shelley and wished him success in his career here.

label: text
text: ASSASSINS AND GENERALS

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Tsingtao, Nov: 9.

label: text
text: Reliable sources report the general retreat of the Fengtien forces following the appearance of Yue Wei-chun's troops.

label: text
text: Hsuchow messages say Honan soldiers are reported to be rapidly advancing and are now not far from Tsinan where a panic pre-vails.

label: text
text: The retreating army is looting extensively.

label: text
text: Local circles are disturbed at the report that 20,000 Fengtien troops are coming by train.

label: text
text: Banks and shops are taking precautions.

label: text
text: The Woosung expedition has been abandoned.

text: JAIL FOR REDS.

label: text
text: The correctional tribunal has sentenced the Communist Moncouau, Secretary of the Unitary General Conference of Labour, Bellenger, Manager of the "Humanité" and three other Communists to eight months' imprisonment and a thousand francs inverior inciting soldiers to insubordination. Two other Communists were sentenced to four months' jail and fine of a thousand francs.

label: paragraph_title
text: SUPERB CHURCH.

label: text
text:
The foundation stone of the magnificent new Episcopal Church of St John the Divine was laid in the presence of church and civic dignatories.
Various objects were buried, including copies of "to-day's newspapers," a Bible and other documents.

Newly brought back yesterday by a Japanese team from Swatow is that the strike pickets are very active preventing any cargo from being worked.
General Chan Kwing-ming's team have added a further defeat while retiring on the Polien border.

label: paragraph_title
text: NEW CHANCELLOR.

label: text
text: HONGKONG UNIVERSITY'S WELCOME.

label: text
text: His Excellency, the Governor being ex officio Chancellor of the University, a meeting of members of the University Union will assemble in the Great Hall tomorrow at 2:30 to welcome the new Chancellor.

label: text
text: The Chairman of the Union will open the meeting with a speech of welcome and a short concert programme will follow, HE the Chancellor addressing the gathering after this. The Vice-Chancellor, Mr. W. W. Hornell, C.I.E. will also speak.

label: text
text:
4 Sir Claud Severn.
On Wednesday, at 8.30 p.m. the University Union will assemble in the Union Assembly room for the purpose of bidding farewell to Sir Claud Severn. The Chairman of the Union will take the chair and there will be two presentations to Sir Claud one from the University Union and the other from the University Union.

label: text
text: Tea will be served after the meeting.
